texts:
Every point on three.ws/globe is open data, and it links back to its source. Conflict, force posture and sanctions are classified from a global news event stream and held in a rolling window, so the time control is real: switching from 7 days to 30 took the map from more than 1,000 points to more than 5,000.

Eleven layers on one globe: conflict, force posture, sanctions, natural events, severe weather, internet outages and economic stress, over military bases, nuclear sites and maritime choke points. None of it needs a key.

Natural events come from the US Geological Survey and NASA, severe weather from the Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System, internet outages from Georgia Tech, and economic stress from World Bank indicators. Ask for more time than the rolling window holds and the layer tells you how much it actually covered, rather than padding the rest.
Press F to flatten the globe into a map, Space to pause the spin. The whole payload is one GET to /api/globe/intel, documented in the globe reference.
